summary.text: Josh Gottheimer is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2016 after a career as a Clinton White House speechwriter and in the private sector, at the Federal Communications Commission, and at Microsoft. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, is Vice-Chair of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, and co-chairs the SALT Caucus. He sought the Democratic nomination for governor in 2025.

paragraphs.text: Born in Livingston, in Essex County, New Jersey, in 1975, and graduated from West Essex Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 2004; between them he studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, on a Thouron Award.

Worked as a speechwriter for President Bill Clinton from 1998 to 2001, including on two State of the Union addresses, and later worked on the presidential campaigns of Wesley Clark and John Kerry in 2004.
Worked in corporate communications at Ford Motor Company and at the public relations firm Burson-Marsteller before joining the Federal Communications Commission in 2010.
Served as senior counselor to the chairman of the FCC and later as a general manager for corporate strategy at Microsoft before running for Congress.
Won the 5th District seat in November 2016, defeating seven-term Republican incumbent Scott Garrett, 51.1% to 46.7%; he was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024.
Serves in Congress on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he is ranking member of the National Security Agency and Cyber Subcommittee, and on the Financial Services Committee.

Helped launch the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus in 2017 and served as co-chair during the 115th through 118th Congresses; now Vice-Chair, and co-chair of the SALT Caucus and the Law Enforcement Caucus.
Announced a run for governor of New Jersey in November 2024 and placed fourth in the June 10, 2025 Democratic primary with 11.8% of the vote.
